question: He receives a 65-year-old man, former smoker with an accumulated consumption of 50 packs / year and diagnosed with emphysema-like COPD. He cites cough with little expectoration and dyspnea of ​​moderate efforts. Request respiratory functional tests. Of the following results, which one is LESS likely?

options.opa: FEV1 (expiratory flow in the first second) less than 80%.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Emphysema-like COPD -> airflow limitation -> decreased FEV1 -> 95% CHAIN: Emphysema-like COPD -> destruction of alveolar walls -> decreased DLCO -> 90% CHAIN: Emphysema-like COPD -> air trapping -> increased TLC -> 85% CHAIN: Emphysema-like COPD -> airway obstruction -> decreased FEV1/FVC ratio -> 95%
enhanced_information: In emphysema-like COPD, the FEV1 is expected to be decreased due to airflow limitation, making option a less likely. The DLCO is typically decreased, so option b is more likely. The FEV1/FVC ratio is usually decreased due to airway obstruction, supporting option c. Air trapping can lead to an increased TLC, making option d more likely.
